CameraMove.description:
A keyed camera move on a generated (moving) beat: the same keys as a frozen moment's camera, but the people keep
walking. The start image is given a depth map, the camera path is flown through it to make a guide video (the
moving subjects softened so they stay free), and the video model generates the beat along that guide, so the camera
does what the keys say instead of what the prompt hopes.

anchor.description: ltx: how firmly the pure-camera render of the start image (the picture flown along the keys) is pinned as keyframes along the way, once a second and at the end. It keeps what things look like and sharpens close-ups (in tests: Laplacian variance 48-63 against 29-48 without, 66 in the pure render) and tightens the camera (0.8% against 1.3% zoom error). 0 = only the first frame is pinned
anchor.title: Anchor

backend.description: What generates the beat along the guide: ltx (LTX-2.3 IC-LoRA depth control, the depth guide a take uses), wan (Wan 2.2 Fun Control, the guide as the control video) or uni3c (Wan Uni3C camera controlnet; needs a model file that is not installed by default). auto: the one measured to follow the keys best (see docs/ENGINE.md)
backend.title: Backend

continues.description: Carry the previous beat's camera across the cut: this beat's camera starts where the previous camera beat ended, with the speed it ended at (no ease to a stop at the boundary), and it starts on that beat's last frame, graded to match

dolly.description: Extra push-in of near things (default follows parallax)

ease.description: How the camera travels between boxes (as `freeze.ease`; `flow` keeps moving through keys)
ease.title: Ease

guide_strength.description: How strongly the guide steers the model (LTX: the IC-LoRA guide strength; Wan: Fun Control has no scale, so this is the Uni3C strength)
guide_strength.title: Guide Strength

keys.description: Camera keys over the beat: {t, box, hold} exactly as in a frozen moment (`freeze.camera`). The camera rests on the first box until its t and on the last after its t
keys.title: Keys

match.description: How far the generated frames are pulled back toward the base plate's tone and grain (the start image of the first beat of the chain, flown along the same camera): a video model drifts in contrast, haze and grain from clip to clip, and a cut shows it. 0 = off. Default: 0.7 for a beat in a chain of `continues` beats, else off
match.title: Match

parallax.description: Depth effect of the guide's camera (as `freeze.parallax`): near things shift against far ones as the camera moves, so the model sees a real camera move

res.description: Size the video model runs at (the frames are scaled to beat_res; ltx: multiples of 64, wan/uni3c: multiples of 16). Default: ltx about 1024x576 (more pixels let the subjects drift in tests; `beat_restore` adds the detail back), wan ~1280x720

Cinemagraph.description:
Make a picture a cinemagraph: a still where only one thing moves (steam from a cup, a curtain in a breeze, light
on water, a candle flame), and everything else is held perfectly still. Put it on any image input (`hero.image`,
a product or strip image, a gallery tile, a section `backdrop`):

    image: { generate: "a cup of coffee, steam rising ...", cinemagraph: { moves: "the steam above the cup" } }

The still stays the picture. The engine finds what moves (Florence-2 + SAM 2.1 from `moves`), has a local video
model (LTX-2.3 or Wan 2.2) bring a crop around it to life, keeps only the moving part, closes the loop and encodes
a small video of that part; the page lays it over the still through a soft mask, so outside the mask the pixels are
the still's and never change. Plain images (no `cinemagraph`) are untouched and keep their cache.

loop.title: Loop

model.description: Video model: ltx (LTX-2.3) or wan (Wan 2.2). Default: the site's video_model, then ltx
model.title: Model

moves.title: Moves

negative_points.title: Negative Points

points.description: Points ON what moves, 0-1 across and down the still
points.title: Points

strength.description: How far it moves: 1 is the motion as generated, lower damps it toward its resting look, higher exaggerates it

FreezeDetail.description:
Deep zoom: the camera may push from the wide shot to a 10-20x close-up and every scale stays sharp. The frame is
not enlarged, it is built into a pyramid of tiles (about `ratio` times the detail per level, as many levels as the
tightest camera box needs): each tile is a crop of its parent, enlarged (SeedVR2), re-drawn at low `strength` so it
gains fine detail in the same style, aligned to its parent, and given the parent's low frequencies exactly, so colours
and shapes agree at every level and only fine detail is new. The render takes each pixel from the finest tile that
covers it and fades levels in by screen-space pixel density, so detail arrives as the camera does and nothing pops.
Every tile is its own cached stage. Needs ComfyUI (SeedVR2, Z-Image Turbo).

Journey.description:
The whole page as one camera journey through one generated world: each stop is a place in it, the camera
travels between them in one unbroken move and the page's content arrives at its stop.

The engine builds it from what it already does best: the first picture is generated from the world and the first
place; every later place is arrived at by a keyed camera move on a moving shot (flown through the picture before,
painted by the video model), then frozen as a moment with a slow parallax while the page holds. Every join is on
the same frame, so there is no cut, and every picture comes out of the one before, so there is no change of style.
The runtime maps scroll to the film: a move plays as you scroll through it, a stop holds while its blocks are read,
and the camera is at rest whenever the page is. On a phone the wide picture is cropped around `focus`; with reduced
motion (or no JavaScript) the page is the stops as stills with their blocks, in order.

blockout.description: The generation approach. Unset: a chain of camera moves between stop pictures (the camera flies through the picture the last stop left, so every stop must be visible in the one before: a facade, a street, a landscape). Set: one continuous take through a blockout of the world (real 3D, so doors and rooms work); every stop then needs a `pose`

JourneyBlockout.description:
The world as rough shapes, as a take's: Blender renders their depth along the camera path, a still of every stop
is painted over that depth (Z-Image Turbo + depth ControlNet) and the video model paints the world between the stops
along the same depth (LTX-2.3). The camera is a real 3D path, so it can go through a door into a room the first
picture never showed; the price is describing the world's layout once, in shapes.

LightScene.description:
Light as the scroll: one place, relit from dawn to night as the page scrolls. The world is one picture (a file, a
generated image, or another scene's still); each time of day is that same picture relit with the geometry locked
(Qwen-Image-Edit, measured and aligned to the world), cached per time. In the browser the scroll moves continuously
through the day: a WebGL shader blends neighbouring times with the light itself (a front of new light spreads from
the sun, shadows sweep, windows and lamps come on one by one with a glow), a slow 2.5D drift lets the place
breathe, and the section's colours (captions, shade) follow the sky. Steps are the sections of the day: each sits at
a time (`state: {time: <id>}`, or in order). Reduced motion shows one still per step.

LightStructure.description:
Geometry lock. The place must not move between times, only the light. Every relight is measured against the world
(how far the editor displaced structure, and how well edges agree); its global move is undone; a relight that is still
too far off is redone with another seed, and the best attempt is kept. What drift is left between neighbouring times
is measured too and the page glides along it (a flow texture) instead of cross-fading doubled edges.

align.description: affine: undo the editor's global move (a few percent of zoom and a few pixels of shift, which is most of what it does to the place) and bend nothing; flow: also pull local structure onto the world with dense optical flow (edges agree better, lines wobble where the editor redrew things; for small drift); none: measure only. What drift remains is glided over in the page

chain.description: Relight each time from its neighbour nearer the world's time instead of from the world: smaller steps of light hold the layout and make neighbouring times agree better, at the price of a little sharpness per step

max_drift.description: How far the place may still be from the world after the global move is undone, mean displacement in pixels at 1024 across; above it the relight is retried with another seed

The prompts are written for 0.85-0.9

Transition.description:
How a section hands over to the next, in the language of film. Without it sections simply follow one another
(today's behaviour). The cut takes its own stretch of scroll (`length`): both pictures are held on screen while the
scroll drives the cut, then the page carries on. Reduced motion, and pages without scripts, get a plain cut.

cut: an instant cut at a scroll position with a held beat either side. dissolve: a held cross-dissolve.
wipe: the next picture is revealed along a line (`direction`, `angle`, `soft`). iris: it opens from a point as a
circle (`origin`, or `closing` for the iris that closes on this one). whip: a fast directional blur-pan into the
next (`direction`, `blur`). match: the end of this section and the start of the next share a shape; the frames scale
and move until the two shapes coincide and the picture swaps on the shape (`shape`, `becomes`). carry: an element
travels from its place here to its place there (`carry`).

angle.description: wipe: the edge's direction in degrees (0 right, 90 down); overrides direction
angle.title: Angle

at.description: cut and match: where in the cut (between the two holds) the picture swaps, 0-1
at.title: At

becomes.description: match: the shape on the next section's first picture (default: the same prompt as `shape`)

blend.description: match: a quick cross-dissolve over the swap, as a share of the stretch (0: a hard swap on the shape)
blend.title: Blend

carry.description: carry: the element that travels (the section's heading to the next one's by default)

closing.description: iris: close on this section (the next shows behind it) instead of opening the next
closing.title: Closing

direction.description: wipe and whip: the way things travel (left: the next picture arrives from the right). Default left
direction.title: Direction

hold.description: The share of the stretch held still at each end, so each picture is on screen a moment before and after the cut
hold.title: Hold

length.description: Scroll distance the cut takes, in screen heights (defaults: cut 0.8, dissolve 1.2, wipe 1.3, iris 1.4, whip 1.1, match 1.5, carry 1.5)
length.title: Length

origin.description: iris: where it opens from, 0-1 across and down the screen (default the middle; with a match, the shape)
origin.title: Origin

shape.description: match: the shape on this section's last picture. Leave out both `shape` and `becomes` to let the engine look for the best-matching pair of shapes (contours)

soft.description: wipe and iris: how soft the edge is (0 hard)
soft.title: Soft

type.description: cut, dissolve, wipe, iris, whip, match or carry
type.title: Type

zoom.description: match: the most each side may be scaled to bring the shapes to the same size (more than this and they only nearly coincide)
zoom.title: Zoom

Wan.description:
Wan 2.2 A14B settings (`video_model: wan`). Two 14B experts sample in turn (high-noise for the first half of
the steps, low-noise for the rest). Renders at ~1280x720, 16 fps, up to 81 frames (~5 s) per clip; longer shots
chain clips from the previous last frame; frames are retimed to 24 fps and restored/upscaled as usual.

WorldPlace.description:
A headline that lives inside the scene. The camera moves and the type goes with the world: it is occluded by what
is nearer, it sits on a surface in perspective, it hangs in the haze. The step's title is the text (its `<em>` words
take the theme's accent as everywhere); `kicker`, `body` and the button stay an ordinary caption beside it. Works on a
film or a sequence with `layout: overlay` and an `at` window on the step (a sequence: the product's own alpha is the
silhouette, so type set behind it is cut exactly), and on a parallax section's step with a photo.
Without WebGL, with reduced motion, and where the headline would be cropped off a narrow screen (a phone held upright),
the title falls back to a clean overlay caption.

align.description: Alignment of a title of several lines
align.title: Align

anchor.description: The frame the thing is found on and the type is laid out on (default: the middle of the step's `at` window). Pick a frame where it is plainly in view

at.title: At

blur.description: Softness of the type in pixels of a 1920-wide frame (behind, sky: default matches how sharp the footage is at that depth)
blur.title: Blur

color.description: auto (light or dark ink, whichever reads on the footage under it), ink, paper, accent, or a hex colour

fog.description: sky: fog in front of the type, thicker low in the picture and where something far passes in front of it

follow.title: Follow

gap.description: behind (named thing): how far behind it the type sits, in depth units
gap.title: Gap

haze.description: How much of the scene's air is mixed into the type (behind: 0.12, sky: 0.5): colour and contrast of distance
haze.title: Haze

kind.description: behind: set at a depth in the scene, so what is nearer (a pine, a railing, a building, a person) passes in front of it as the camera moves; surface: painted on a wall, a sign or a floor, tracked to it in perspective, with the surface's light and texture showing through; sky: large type in the haze at far depth, with fog in front

slant.title: Slant

track.description: Letter-spacing in em (default: 0 behind, 0.05 on a surface, 0.1 in the sky)

track_model.description: How the footage is followed: a surface is tracked as a plane seen in perspective (homography); behind and sky as a layer that shifts, turns and zooms (similarity)
track_model.title: Track Model
